function: NN estimates the wideband IRS-cascaded channel autocorrelation matrix from user RSRP measurements without pilots; classical SDR-based optimization then designs the reflection (p. 1, 8).
system: Downlink OFDM, single-antenna BS and user, passive IRS of 4x8=32 elements with 2-bit phase shifts, 128 subcarriers; carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Supervised learning of a single-layer NN made of K' subnetworks, trained by SGD on RSRP labels; progressive training adds subnetworks until validation MSE converges (p. 2, 6-7).
data_channel: Own simulator: BS-user and BS-IRS i.i.d. Rayleigh with exponential delay profile, IRS-user Rician (7 dB), path loss citing 3GPP TS 25.996; 1000 channel realizations (p. 9-10).
test_conditions: NN trained on RSRP samples of each setup (training/validation split of L random reflections); NMSE over 1000 channel realizations; also N=128, five users, other decay factors (p. 7, 9-12).
baselines: RMS and CSM [37] (non-learned), perfect-CSI upper bound, NN with rank-one approximation (earlier narrowband NN [38], [39]), NN with true rank (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE of the autocorrelation estimate; average channel power gain (dB); OFDM achievable rate (bps/Hz); training MSE versus number of subnetworks (p. 9-12).
q1_support: p. 9: "The CIR coefficients for each link are generated based on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading" - custom simulator; 3GPP TS 25.996 [54] is cited only for path loss and the Rician factor; no TR 38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "independently training a NN for each user to reconstruct their respective IRS channel autocorrelation matrices" - the NN is fitted anew on each setup (N=128, five users, decay factors); no test in a condition unseen in training is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "we adopt the random-max sampling (RMS) [37], [57] and CSM [37] methods as benchmark schemes"; p. 10: "reduces to that for estimating the narrowband rank-one IRS channel autocorrelation matrix [38], [39]"
q4_support: p. 5: "can be solved with a significantly reduced complexity" - qualitative only; no complexity order, operation count or runtime of the proposed method is reported (the O(N^2) on p. 5 refers to estimating the full matrix).
q5_support: p. 9: "The CIR coefficients for each link are generated based on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading" - self-generated simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset are stated.
notes: Area 2: the learned part is the NN estimating the channel autocorrelation matrix (NMSE, Fig. 6); the reflection design that follows is SDR plus successive refinement, not learned (p. 8). The NN is fitted online per channel realization from RSRP samples, so its weights are the channel factors; included because the paper frames it as supervised NN training (p. 2). q3 is borderline: the K'=1 benchmark is a variant of the proposed network but the paper identifies it with the earlier narrowband NN of the same authors [38], [39] (p. 6 footnote 1, p. 10); reviewer to confirm it is not only an ablation. q4: the weight count (2N+2 per subnetwork, p. 7) is stated only as model structure, not as a cost, so it is not counted.
